title: Extract Culprit Hosts
description: Extracts the culprit hosts that the runtime names explicitly in its own logs. Pathways: 'lost connection to peer at http://machine/<node>', '<node> exiting'. McJax / MaxText / Megascale multi-slice (signature_family megascale|barrier): the Megascale hang digest 'Potential culprit workers: <worker>:<host>' (megascale_culprits), and JAX coordination-service 'Barrier timed out ... Some timed out task names' / 'Task <t> heartbeat timeout' (non_arriving_tasks, mapped to candidate pod/node; the timeout is the victim, the non-arriving task is the lead). earliest_error_candidates ranks pods by their EARLIEST crash line (never worker 0 or the loudest pod by default). For Pathways it collapses each host death into a single incident, and separates genuine failures from teardown cascade by reporting breadth. Attribution MUST be quoted from these lines rather than inferred from DATA_LOSS device coordinates, which identify where the symptom surfaced and often point at a different slice than the host that died. Node Replacement is decided on distinct PRIMARY incidents, never on raw event count. Reads retry with backoff on Cloud Logging quota (429/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED) and 503; status is COMPLETE, INCOMPLETE (a query failed or hit --limit; failures listed in query_errors) or NO_DATA (every query failed), and signature_family is 'unknown' rather than 'none' unless status is COMPLETE.

limit.description: Per-term log read cap; the script warns loudly if a term saturates it, since truncation biases attribution.

cluster_seconds.description: Same-node events within this window count as ONE incident (window anchored to the first event, so a drip of retry lines cannot chain).

min_reporting_pods.description: Distinct reporting pods required to classify an incident as primary rather than teardown cascade.

cluster_name.description: Optional exact GKE cluster name; narrows every scan via an indexed resource label.

namespace.description: Optional exact Kubernetes namespace; narrows every scan via an indexed resource label.

slice_minutes.description: Concurrent slice width in minutes; 0 = auto (360 for windows over one day, else a single query). Truncation is reported per slice.
